proof.criterion: A reader resuming from a cursor never misses an event that commits later with a lower id; a test commits two writes out of id order and a resuming reader gets both in a defined order.
proof.surface: GET /api/v1/events (SSE) cold and with Last-Event-ID, on one and two envoy-dispatch processes; newly started processes while a transaction holds an id
proof.command: adv.py ooo commit; adv.py ooo rollback; adv.py concurrent; STREAM_PORT=17778 adv.py concurrent; adv.py fresh resume|cold; adv.py heartbeat; adv.py shutdown <pid>; adv.py churn 30; adv.py stall; adv.py lastid
proof.observed: Lower id 123 was open while the higher 124 committed. The stream sent nothing, then 123 and 124 after the commit, and a resume sent the same. On rollback the stream sent only 124, 37 ms after. Concurrency: 80 POSTs and 16 slow writes, 4 of them rolled back. Each of 3 streams got exactly the 92 committed ids in order, as did a mid-run resume, on one process and with the streams on a second process. Newly started process with a foreign id held: a resuming stream opened in 14 ms, heartbeat twice in 35 s, and got the held-back event 26 ms after the commit. SIGTERM exited in 0.05 s and ended the stream. Four staggered 2 s id holders overlapped for 30 s: every frame arrived 1.8 to 2.1 s after its write, so the horizon kept advancing. A foreign 8 s hold delayed the frame until 186 ms after the commit. Bad Last-Event-ID values are refused 400, and a resume from 0 equals the database.
proof.negativeControl: Main c210f10d: the open stream sent 124 at once and never 123. In the concurrency run each stream missed 10 committed ids ([131, 132, 137, 138, 148, 153, 159, 172, 177, 185]), and the resume missed 7.

proof.criterion: Every consumer of the event stream keeps the order it relies on; the plan lists each and the test covers each.

proof.observed: References: the first since read on a quiet, newly started process, right after a mention committed, listed it in 50 ms, which fixes the reviewer's finding on Safe. With a foreign id held, the read answered in 1,009 ms without the newer mention and listed it once the holder ended. With a lower id open, it withheld the higher mention, then listed it after the commit. NATS: 30 concurrent comments on TSB-51 reached its subject in seq order, 2 to 31, equal to the database. The delivery hub has no reachable surface on this stack (it needs delivery settings proven against the GitHub App), so it rests on its Go tests, which CI has not run at this head.
